name: Question 14
problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[35−1403−1−42]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[50−4], [34−1], and [−132]
b
[34−1], [−450], and [32−1]
c
[34−1], [50−4], and [−132]
d
[−1−42], [403], and [35−1]
e
[35−1], [403], and [−1−42]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[34−1]T(j)=T[010]=[50−4]T(k)=T[001]=[−132]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[35−1403−1−42][100]=[34−1]T(j)=T⋅j=[35−1403−1−42][010]=[50−4]T(k)=T⋅k=[35−1403−1−42][001]=[−132]
